\[
r_s = \frac{r\, (1 + k\, r^2)}{1 + k},
\qquad k = 0.3
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(r\): The distance of an output pixel from the image center, as a share of half the diagonal
- \(r_s\): The distance of the source position it reads, in the same unit
- \(k\): The strength of the radial term

The source radius grows faster than the output radius toward the edges, so the outer part of the image is squeezed inward and straight lines through it bow outward. The factor 1 + k r^2 is the first radial term of the lens distortion model that camera calibration uses, as in OpenCV. Keep corners divides by 1 + k so that the corners, at r = 1, read from the corners. Without it, the divisor is 1 and the edges read from outside the image. Each output pixel reads the source at the mapped position with bilinear interpolation, the inverse mapping of Gonzalez and Woods, so no holes appear.
